body:
Watches live 72h now, and each one was read every minute for all of it (4,320 reads), with the resident server awake every 15s the whole time. This reads a watch at **1/24 of how long it has been quiet, clamped to [1m, 60m]**, and lets the server sleep until the next watch is due.

## What changed

- **The schedule** is one pure function, [`read_every`](https://github.com/dpep/inkling/blob/702647e/src/adapters/watches_json.rs#L61), with its constants named. "Quiet since" is a new `stirred_at` on each watch: set on registration, on every re-registration (a touch: `post-tool` seeing `gh pr …` / a `git push` that names it, or `inkling watch`), and on a transition. [`Watch::next_read`](https://github.com/dpep/inkling/blob/702647e/src/adapters/watches_json.rs#L146) is measured from the last reading, so it's a fixed instant everyone agrees on. A poll reads only [`due_now`](https://github.com/dpep/inkling/blob/702647e/src/adapters/watches_json.rs#L349).
- **The server sleeps until the next watch is due.** A tick returns a `Beat` (pulse + when it next wants to run); [`Serve::nap`](https://github.com/dpep/inkling/blob/702647e/src/serve.rs#L480) sleeps until then, never shorter than `interval` (15s, so an unreadable watch can't spin) and never past the idle or lifetime deadline.
- **A doorbell wakes it.** Nothing woke a running server early before this; the 15s tick was the wake. The server now listens on a FIFO, `serve.wake`, beside its lock ([`Doorbell`](https://github.com/dpep/inkling/blob/702647e/src/serve.rs#L550)). [`ensure_serving`](https://github.com/dpep/inkling/blob/702647e/src/main.rs#L1366) (`watch`, `post-tool`, `subscribe`) [rings it](https://github.com/dpep/inkling/blob/702647e/src/serve.rs#L617) before deciding whether to spawn. If the FIFO can't be made, naps are capped at the interval, which is the old cadence.
- **`--refresh` is a floor under the schedule.** `events --refresh D` and the prompt hook (60s) read only what the schedule says is due, and never a reading younger than `D`. Using the shorter of the two would put everything back on one-minute reads whenever someone was typing. The reasoning is in [watching.md, "How often a watch is read"](https://github.com/dpep/inkling/blob/702647e/docs/watching.md#how-often-a-watch-is-read).
- **`inkling status`** has a new `upstream` line in `last 24h`: pull request reads, GitHub queries, Jira reads, and reads per transition. `polled watches` now logs `github=` / `jira=`. See [`per_transition`](https://github.com/dpep/inkling/blob/702647e/src/main.rs#L2080).
- **[docs/deferred.md](https://github.com/dpep/inkling/blob/702647e/docs/deferred.md#tuning-how-often-a-watch-is-read)** records the rule as a placeholder: what was measured, and what would change it.
- **Separate last commit:** the server stands down when a new build is installed over the binary it was started from ([`build_of`](https://github.com/dpep/inkling/blob/702647e/src/serve.rs#L532): dev, inode and mtime of the launch path, checked every tick). Found live: after `make install` of #16, the old server pushed `#17 state draft → open`, which #16 had stopped pushing.

## Numbers

- One watch that never moves: **~170 reads over 72h** instead of 4,320. That's 24 at the one-minute floor, ~98 while backing off, then 48 hourly (`three_quiet_days_cost_under_two_hundred_reads_not_four_thousand`).
- The table in the brief was loose: the one-minute floor lasts **24 minutes**, not an hour. An hour quiet is already 2.5 minutes. I kept the rule as stated.
- The cost: news on a PR nobody has touched for a day can be up to an hour late.

## Proof, end to end

Fake clock: the schedule table, backoff over 72h, a touch snapping back to 1m, a transition resetting quiet, due-only batches, the floor, and legacy files without `stirred_at` (watches_json tests). Serve-loop spacing, the interval floor, the idle and lifetime bounds, and the doorbell itself on a real FIFO (serve tests).

Scratch server (debug build, scratch paths, a throwaway draft PR on dpep/inkling-ci-probe, now closed):

- Fresh watch: reads at 03:21:54, 03:22:54, `nap_seconds=59`.
- Backdated `stirred_at` by 30h, restarted: `next=04:22:53`, `nap_seconds=3560`.
- Touched through `inkling hook post-tool` at 03:23:42: the server woke **the same millisecond** on the ring, then read at 03:23:57, 03:24:57, 03:25:57.
- The first run found a real bug: the nap was rounded down to whole milliseconds, so the server woke 0.4ms before the watch was due, found nothing due, and lost 15s. Fixed in "Round a nap up, not down".
- Replaced build: started a server from a copied binary, renamed a new copy over it at 03:26:22. It logged `a new build was installed; standing down` at its next wake (03:27:20) and exited `reason="replaced"`. On macOS `current_exe()` gave the launch path, so stat-ing it sees the new file.

## What I couldn't verify

- 24h+ of real backoff, and whether the ratio in `status` looks sane after a week. That's what deferred.md asks for.
- Push to an attached session while the server is on a long nap. The scratch run had no attached subscriber, so the pulse was `idle` (I raised `idle_after` to 12h to keep it up). The nap and doorbell code paths don't depend on the pulse.
- A replaced binary is only noticed when the server wakes: within its current nap, which is at most an hour and is cut short by the next watch change. `make install` doesn't ring.

## Dogfood

- Rung 1: `inkling wait --until checks dpep/inkling#18` (installed build, which has #17) started 5s after `gh pr create` and answered `success … met after 1m 2s (5 polls)`. No false preclusion right after opening. I could act on it without a further lookup.
- Rungs 3–4: this was opened from a subagent, and its `gh pr create` auto-watched #18 on the **parent** session. Any push went there, not to me, so I can't report its latency from here.
- The installed build still ticks every 15s. None of this is live until `make install` after merge, and the new server behavior will only be dogfooded from then on.
